snapshot(TASK-20260826-9e9d53): bind BATCH-762807's opening and producer package before review

Snapshot archive for GOAL-MLKEM-005 BATCH-762807, sources TASK-20260826-f1340b
and TASK-20260826-602395, question RQ-MLKEM-001. Makes the reviewed object fixed
before either reviewer reads it, per docs/dynamic-subagent-dispatch.md: a
producer must not be its own sole interpreter, and a review of a moving target
is not a review.

Binds 23 of the archive's 24 declared paths by sha256 -- the opening control
plane, the producer's instrument, acceptance suite and evidence, and the review
plan with both sibling-blind assignments. The 24th is this receipt, which does
NOT hash itself: a hash written inside the bytes it hashes can never match them.
It is bound by the queue's archive block instead -- mutual, never self.
dispatch_queue.json is bound by nothing and is in no task's artifact_paths, for
the same structural reason, and that residual is disclosed rather than papered
over with an uncheckable value.

binding_mode content_first, declared at opening rather than retrofitted. The
bound bytes landed across three commits -- d26d0e77f the opening, 2337c15b4 the
producer package, 594c337c8 the review plan -- because this container is
ephemeral and holding finished artifacts uncommitted to satisfy a one-commit
rule would risk losing them. content_first binds every declared byte at HEAD and
still requires a reachable commit, a matching parent and the record IDs in the
message. The binding to one commit is relaxed; the binding to bytes is not.

12 further files are disclosed as staged-not-in-binding-set: the
failed_infrastructure surrogate sets from a real SIGTERM and a real timeout, and
the tiny-cell set, committed under DEC-20260815-3e8e9c condition (v), which
forbids directing their deletion. They were not declared at opening, so they are
disclosed here rather than dropped for being undeclared or smuggled into the
binding set after the fact.

WHAT THIS ARCHIVE DOES NOT ASSERT: that the instrument is correct, that its
fixes work at d=512, or that anything here is evidence about ML-KEM at any
standardized parameter set. A snapshot makes bytes durable so that independent
review reads a fixed object. It is not a review and it is not a result.

Rule 12 UNMET AND UNWAIVED. Independence in this round is procedural -- fresh
sessions, disjoint write scopes, sibling blindness, a plan written before either
reviewer ran, a sealed prior, and a blinded quantity that no artifact carries --
and never model-level.

Binds 7 of the archive's 8 declared paths by sha256: both reviewers' reports and
attestations, the evidence record, the decision record, and the goal head. The
8th is this receipt, which does not hash itself -- the queue binds it instead.
binding_mode content_first, declared at opening.

84 FILES ARE DISCLOSED BY NAME AS STAGED-NOT-IN-BINDING-SET, and this is the one
judgement in the close that both reviewers explicitly demanded be made
explicitly rather than by default. They are the reviewers' probe evidence and
the Validator's phase-0 blind-rederivation.yaml. They were undeclared at opening
and are therefore ineligible for path_sha256, which the dispatcher requires to
be a subset of declared artifact_paths -- declaring them now would be
retrofitting scope after the fact.

They are nonetheless COMMITTED AND DURABLE, landed at d73558cb4, 2a36fe06f and
ab6de4703. Among them are the RAW KILL-MATRIX JOURNALS -- ten real-subprocess
scenarios including SIGKILL, a 30-signal storm against a 1 ms heartbeat, a
startup race and a between-cells kill -- which EXIST NOWHERE ELSE and are the
only primary record behind the J2 verdict. They are bound by nothing. That is
stated plainly rather than papered over with a value no receipt could check, and
the successor batch should declare its reviewers' probe trees at opening so this
choice does not recur.

rule_12_status records both problems, not one: every role resolves to a single
model, AND commit d73558cb4 carried one reviewer's joint verdicts in its subject
while its sibling was still writing, which git log exposed. The two ADMIT WITH
NAMED RESIDUAL rulings are therefore not independent corroboration of each
other. All 80 of the Validator's probe and derivation files predate that commit
and none follow it, so its evidence base was complete before the exposure; its
write-up was not.

WHAT THIS ARCHIVE DOES NOT ASSERT: that the instrument is correct at d=512, that
its residuals are closed, or that anything here is evidence about ML-KEM at any
standardized parameter set. Claim ceiling instrument_repair, claim tier toy,
evidence strength preliminary, no hypothesis moved.
